# Volume 2 — VIII Thirza Adopts Twins

!!! note "Source text"
    Passages cited on the wiki pages link into this page. Only volumes at or before
    this page's cutoff are present.

Mrs. Agatha Sowerby was positioned by the window of her kitchen, working on a quilt with her knitting needles, in the exact same manner she had been seated a few years before on a particular evening when Obed Abernethy had come driving down the hill bringing along the person Mrs. Agatha described as “his imported orphan.” However, that prior occasion occurred during the spring season; whereas the current time was the end of autumn, with the fields faded to brown and every tree in the forests stripped of leaves. The sun was in the process of going down in a grand display of gold and purple splendor beyond the black forests to the west of Brierley as a buggy pulled by a gentle brown horse traveled down the incline. Mrs. Agatha looked closely and intently toward it.
{: #nw-v02-c08-p0000 }

“Thirza is arriving back from the funeral,” she remarked to her spouse, who was resting on the couch in the kitchen. Thomas Sowerby spent a greater amount of time on the couch lately than was his former habit, though Mrs. Agatha, despite her keenness for observing matters outside her own home, had failed to observe this so far. “And both the twins are with her, . . . indeed, Robin is bent over the dashboard attempting to seize the pony’s tail while Thirza pulls him backward. Lucy sits upon the bench as neat as can be. She constantly appears as though she was recently starched and ironed. Ah well, unfortunate Thirza will certainly have her time completely occupied this winter. Even so, I fail to see how she could have done otherwise than accept them, given the situation, and Nell will assist her. Nell is utterly delighted about the entire affair, and she possesses a truly clever knack with youngsters, I have to admit. Goodness, it feels like only yesterday that poor Obed returned home with Nell herself and everyone mocked the thought of Thirza raising a youngster. Now she has taken in twins. A person is never secure against being astonished until they pass away.”
{: #nw-v02-c08-p0001 }

The rotund pony trotted across the bridge located in Sowerby’s Hollow before continuing down the Grey Shutters lane. Thirza wore a somewhat stern expression. East Welby lay ten miles behind them, and an obsession with endless movement appeared to hold Robin Farrow in its grip. Thirza lacked the ability to compel his stillness, and throughout the entire journey she endured severe anxiety that he might tumble off the wagon's rear to snap his neck, or pitch across the dashboard beneath the pony’s hooves. Desperate at last, she warned that she would give him a thorough whipping once she brought him home. At this, Robin scrambled onto her lap without care for the reins, wrapped his plump arms around her neck, and embraced her fiercely like a bear.
{: #nw-v02-c08-p0002 }

“I don’t believe you mean it,” he said, tapping her lined cheek in a fond way. “You do not seem like the kind of lady who would lash a small boy simply because he was unable to stay motionless. Did you not find staying motionless terribly difficult when you were merely as old as I am?”
{: #nw-v02-c08-p0003 }

“No, I constantly remained motionless whenever I received orders,” Thirza stated, attempting to sound firm, even though she sensed her inner feelings growing gentle beneath the spontaneous affection of Robin.
{: #nw-v02-c08-p0004 }

“Well, I reckon that happened since you used to be a girl,” Robin stated, wriggling returning to where he had been following one more embrace. “I reckon you used to be a girl at one time, even if considering it is terribly strange. Lucy is able to remain seated without moving . . . yet I do not believe there is a lot of enjoyment in that. It appears to me that being a girl has to be dull. Here, Lucy, allow me to make you a little more lively.”
{: #nw-v02-c08-p0005 }

To “liven up” Lucy, Robin’s approach involved clutching her curls with his fingers and pulling them. Lucy let out a shriek and subsequently wept.
{: #nw-v02-c08-p0006 }

“In what way can you act like such a wicked child when your unfortunate mother was placed in her plot only today?” asked Thirza in desperation.
{: #nw-v02-c08-p0007 }

“However, she felt happy to pass away,” Robin whispered in secret. “I am certain of it, since she informed me herself. Sickly for so long, she had grown extremely weary of it. On the evening prior to her passing, we had a lengthy conversation. She mentioned to me that you were planning to care for Lucy and me throughout the winter, and that I must behave myself. I intend to behave, yet is it not possible to behave while racing about just as easily as while remaining seated? Furthermore, she instructed that I must constantly show kindness to Lucy and defend her, and that is my intention.”
{: #nw-v02-c08-p0008 }

“Is yanking her hair what you consider being nice to her?”
{: #nw-v02-c08-p0009 }

“Well, no one else is going to be allowed to pull it by me,” Robin stated, clenching his hands into fists and scowling. “It would be better if they didn't even attempt it. She wasn't hurt much by me . . . her crying was simply because she is a girl. Being a boy makes me glad, though being a twin makes me sorry. Whenever Jimmy Sprott gets contradicted by his sister, his only response is, ‘Because I’m your senior, it follows that I know better,’ which puts an end to her arguments. However, Lucy cannot be told that by me, so she simply continues to hold opinions that differ from mine. Given that I am a man, the gee-gee could be driven by me for a little while.”
{: #nw-v02-c08-p0010 }

On the whole, Thirza felt a sense of gratitude as she entered her personal yard, in which the autumnal night breeze pranced among the brown leaves. Waiting at the gate to greet the arrivals and hoist the twins down was Nell. While Lucy quietly allowed herself to be kissed, Robin returned Nell's greeting by giving her a enthusiastic embrace and merrily declaring, “I’m Mr. Robin Farrow.”
{: #nw-v02-c08-p0011 }

While Lucy conducted herself in the manner of a proper young woman during the evening meal, the behavior of Robin was far from acceptable.
{: #nw-v02-c08-p0012 }

“I am so starved that there is no time for me to eat with manners,” he remarked upon being chided by Thirza. “Lucy is not nearly as starved as me. Consider the vast amount of exercise I got during the trip to this place. The cake is exceptionally delicious and filled with raisins. There has not been any cake at our house for an extremely long time, because mother was excessively ill to bake it and Mrs. Sprott stated that baking our bread for us was the absolute limit of what she could manage. Furthermore, Mrs. Wiggins fails to ever include raisins in her cakes. Not a chance with her! May I get a second slice?”
{: #nw-v02-c08-p0013 }

Although Thirza wished to decline, Nell served a substantial additional piece. Even so, she prompted Robin that he should utter “Thank you” in response to it. Robin simply smiled widely at her and swallowed a massive mouthful. After he completed the piece he remarked,
{: #nw-v02-c08-p0014 }

“I shall express my gratitude if you hand me one more portion.”
{: #nw-v02-c08-p0015 }

“No, you have consumed sufficient cake,” declared Thirza, utilizing an intonation that Nell recognized and Robin would come to realize permitted no debate.
{: #nw-v02-c08-p0016 }

Robin offered a wink to Nell, after which he bent across the board, grabbed the initial portion of cake belonging to Lucy, who had merely had a single delicate small nip of it, directly from her own hands and, parting his jaws as wide as possible, stuffed the entire piece inside. A quiver came to Lucy’s lip and Thirza found herself unable to speak from shock. Nell immediately declared, assuming her finest “schoolma’am” manner,
{: #nw-v02-c08-p0017 }

“Oh, Robin, men of quality would never act in such a manner.”
{: #nw-v02-c08-p0018 }

“I’m aware that they don’t,” Robin uttered, the moment he was able to talk, “yet I’m no gemplum.”
{: #nw-v02-c08-p0019 }

“However, wouldn't you prefer to become one?” inquired a surprised Nell.
{: #nw-v02-c08-p0020 }

“Naturally I do. However, becoming a gemplum is impossible until you are older.”
{: #nw-v02-c08-p0021 }

“Oh, indeed you can,” Nell hastened to say, believing she noticed an opportunity to sow good seed early. “You can start being a gentleman while you are a young boy. And gentlemen never grab things from ladies . . . or neglect to say thank you . . . or yank anyone’s hair.”
{: #nw-v02-c08-p0022 }

“It’s a certainty that they fail to enjoy themselves very much,” Robin stated openly. “I suppose I will hold off on becoming one until I reach adulthood.”
{: #nw-v02-c08-p0023 }

A further slice of cake was sliced for Lucy by a resigned Thirza. Robin was someone she lacked the energy to deal with at that time. Between the funeral service and the extensive journey by car, the day had proven taxing for her. Right then, her outlook on what lay ahead was marked by a gloominess that would have rivaled Eliza Pullen’s own.
{: #nw-v02-c08-p0024 }

Despite both being fair-haired, the twins did not look strikingly similar. The long, sleek curls that Lucy possessed were always perfectly neat. A head of tiny, fuzzy yellow ringlets covered Robin’s round skull. Gentle and mild hazel eyes belonged to Lucy, whereas Robin’s danced with an elfish roguishness. While Lucy had a straight nose, Robin’s was undeniably snubbed; Lucy’s mouth was set in a “prunes and prisms” expression, but Robin’s was perpetually smiling; moreover, a single dimple indented one of his cheeks, giving him a sweet, amusing, uneven appearance whenever he chuckled. Every detail of his small face seemed to harbor joy and playfulness.
{: #nw-v02-c08-p0025 }

“The best option is for them to turn in,” remarked Thirza, believing that this was the simplest manner of dealing with them. “Lucy is going to share my bed, whereas Robin can be accommodated by you in the west gable. Sleeping by yourself doesn't frighten you, does it, Robin?”
{: #nw-v02-c08-p0026 }

“No; however, I am not planning on turning in for a very long time still,” Robin remarked in a relaxed manner.
{: #nw-v02-c08-p0027 }

“Indeed, you are.” The sorely tested Thirza uttered nothing more than those words, yet the quality of her voice silenced Robin himself. Beside Nell, he hurried dutifully up the stairs.
{: #nw-v02-c08-p0028 }

“The moment I become an adult, my absolute highest priority will be remaining awake through an entire night simply to discover how it feels,” he secretly confided to her.
{: #nw-v02-c08-p0029 }

In subsequent years Thirza could not recall that initial week of the twins' stay at Grey Shutters without shivering. It was not that it was actually significantly worse than the weeks that came after; rather, it appeared that way because it was new. Hardly a single conscious minute of any day passed in which Robin was not engaged in mischief or planning it; however, his first remarkable feat took place two days following his arrival, on Sunday morning . . . a lovely, warm day, which was as hazy and gentle as September. While Thirza took care of Lucy, Nell got him ready for church. Initially, Robin resisted forcefully when his face was being washed.
{: #nw-v02-c08-p0030 }

“Thirza did the laundry yesterday . . . and Mrs. Wiggins scrubbed my skin using hard soap on the funeral day. For a single week, that suffices. Being so exceedingly clean seems pointless to me. Staying dirty is far more comfortable.”
{: #nw-v02-c08-p0031 }

“With no need for prompting, Cedric Stanhope cleans his face daily,” observed Nell cleverly.
{: #nw-v02-c08-p0032 }

Robin had resided at Grey Shutters for just a bit more than forty-eight hours; yet his adoration for Nell and his hatred for Cedric Stanhope, whom Nell had been heard praising with great enthusiasm the day following his arrival, were already established. Should Cedric Stanhope wash his face daily, the matter was decided. He, Robin Farrow, would likewise perform the act, even if it proved fatal to him. This very thought persuaded him to yield quietly to the remaining aspects of his grooming, and he truly appeared as an attractive young boy once everything was completed. Nell experienced a feeling of nearly motherly pride regarding him while she escorted him to the ancient Abernethy pew.
{: #nw-v02-c08-p0033 }

Initially, Robin acted rather decently, as he was busy stealing secret looks at every young boy in sight and trying to guess which one might be Cedric Stanhope. Nothing out of the ordinary occurred during the initial pair of hymns or the reading of the Scripture. It was while Mr. Wace was offering a prayer that the stir took place.
{: #nw-v02-c08-p0034 }

Directly ahead of Robin sat Lauretta White, whose head leaned forward a bit while her blonde hair dangled in a pair of lengthy plaits, framing an alluring stretch of pale neck that was enveloped by a relaxed frill of lace. Lauretta was an eight-year-old child, plump and serene in appearance, who had behaved faultlessly during services ever since the initial occasion when her mother brought her to church as a six-month-old baby.
{: #nw-v02-c08-p0035 }

Reaching into his pocket, Robin pulled out . . . a caterpillar, one that was furry and squirming. Thirza caught sight of it and made a grab for him, yet she acted too late. Down Lauretta’s neck, Robin let the caterpillar fall.
{: #nw-v02-c08-p0036 }

A succession of sharp screams shattered the exact center of Mr. Wace’s prayer. Horrified, the minister ceased praying and unclosed his eyes. All the heads throughout the assembly snapped upward. In her pew, Lauretta White was leaping up and down while wildly grabbing at the rear of her dress.
{: #nw-v02-c08-p0037 }

“Ouch . . . mother . . . mother . . . ouch . . . remove it . . . ouch . . . pull it out . . . ouch . . . that naughty child stuffed it inside my collar . . . ouch . . . mother . . . it is slipping deeper down . . . ouch . . . ouch . . . ouch. . . .”
{: #nw-v02-c08-p0038 }

Mrs. White got up and, her countenance resolute, bore the weeping, twisting Lauretta away from the church. As her screams faded into the distance, Mr. Wace continued reading the liturgy. Yet each person sensed that the day's proceedings were ruined. Thirza ignored the sermon for the very first time in her existence, and Nell remained seated, her face flushed red with shame.
{: #nw-v02-c08-p0039 }

After they arrived at their house, Thirza placed Robin in bed, forcing him to remain there through the remainder of the day. Refusing to feed him any dinner, she only permitted him a simple tea consisting of bread and milk. Nell brought this meal up to him and waited sadly beside him as he consumed it with a remorseless delight. Nevertheless, Nell’s sorrowful gaze made him feel uneasy.
{: #nw-v02-c08-p0040 }

“I reckon,” he mused thoughtfully, “that Cedric Stanhope wouldn’t have put a caterpillar down a girl’s neck during a church service, would he?”
{: #nw-v02-c08-p0041 }

“He truly would not,” Nell remarked with sorrow.
{: #nw-v02-c08-p0042 }

“Well, I suppose I regret doing it, in that case,” Robin admitted. “However, the caterpillar was so amazingly large . . . I grabbed him from the church steps right as we entered. Wasting him appeared to be a shame. Also, tell me, was it not amusing listening to that girl scream?”
{: #nw-v02-c08-p0043 }

On Tuesday afternoon, Grey Shutters hosted the gathering of the Aid Society. Nell rushed back from school, aware that Thirza required every bit of help she was able to provide. Lucy, immaculate and genteel in a crisp, starched white dress accented by a black sash, sat among the Aid's attendees inside the parlor, answering modestly whenever addressed, remaining quiet otherwise, and behaving in all respects like an exemplary youth. Robin, delightfully coated in dirt, fashioned mud pies out in the barnyard.
{: #nw-v02-c08-p0044 }

“I said he could,” Thirza remarked with fatigue. “My belief was that it would prevent him from doing something worse. Getting muddy is the only harm there. Before we summon him for his tea, we will finish ours. Lucy is allowed to join us for hers, though I would not have the courage to permit Robin to take a seat at the table while all the Aids are present.”
{: #nw-v02-c08-p0045 }

Going to summon the Aids for tea, Nell discovered that Lucy was missing from the parlor. Mrs. Jasper Bell mentioned that Robin had arrived at the front entrance and asked her to step outside. Following a brief discussion with Thirza in the pantry, they decided that both children should be given their tea together at a later time.
{: #nw-v02-c08-p0046 }

The midway mark of tea had passed when an unhappy shape burst into the dining room. Dismay filled the gazes of Thirza and Nell, while astonishment took hold of the Aids. Might that truly be Lucy . . . that weeping, indistinct person clad in a soaked, trickling dress, her hair shedding streams of water onto Thirza’s new coin-spot rug?
{: #nw-v02-c08-p0047 }

“Lucy, what has happened to you?” exclaimed Nell, glancing guiltily toward Mrs. Jasper Bell, who belonged to what was reputedly the sole family on earth that never suffered accidents.
{: #nw-v02-c08-p0048 }

“Robin forced me to balance on the pigpen fence,” sobbed Lucy. “I refused at first, but he taunted me by calling me a fraid-cat. Then I tumbled down inside the pigpen, which ruined my dress with dirt, and the pig charged straight across me. Even though my dress looked terrible, Robin promised to spray it clean if I stood beneath the pump, so I obeyed him and he drenched me with water, yet my dress remains just as dirty, while my beautiful shoes and sash are completely ruined.”
{: #nw-v02-c08-p0049 }

For the remainder of the dinner, Nell performed the table's duties by herself, during which time Thirza went up to the higher floor and put Lucy back into her previous garments. Robin was captured and dispatched to his room for the night deprived of any evening meal. At dusk, Nell visited his bedchamber and spoke to him in a solemn manner . . . an approach in which she placed immense trust, one that the outcomes did not entirely fail to warrant. She informed him that his behavior made her feel deeply upset.
{: #nw-v02-c08-p0050 }

“Now I feel sorry myself,” Robin conceded, “however the problem is that I am never sorry about doing things until I have done them. Because she was scared of dirtying her clo’es, Lucy refused to assist me in making pies, which made me extremely angry. If Cedric Stanhope had known his sister would fall in, I suppose he would not have forced her to walk a pigpen fence?”
{: #nw-v02-c08-p0051 }

“No, such a thought would never cross his mind. Cedric is an absolute little gentleman.”
{: #nw-v02-c08-p0052 }

Robin squeezed his eyes closed completely and appeared to contemplate the matter briefly. After that, he crept upward and wrapped his arms around Nell’s neck, nestling his warm, small face against her shoulder.
{: #nw-v02-c08-p0053 }

“Nell, isn't there a little bit of affection you have for me, even though I'm not a good boy like Cedric?”
{: #nw-v02-c08-p0054 }

“I certainly do,” Nell stated with genuine feeling. For some reason, she found it impossible not to hold a fond affection for Robin. “Even so, my fondness for you would grow if your mischievous behavior ceased.”
{: #nw-v02-c08-p0055 }

“I . . . performed another action today,” Robin continued, his voice muted. “I regret it at this moment, but I am terribly frightened to inform you. You will not become too angry, will you? And you will not inform Thirza, will you?”
{: #nw-v02-c08-p0056 }

“I’m uncertain, Robin. It might be best if I inform her. However, I believe I can give you my word that I will abstain, provided you give me your word that you will abstain from ever repeating it, no matter what it might be.”
{: #nw-v02-c08-p0057 }

“No, I never will,” I replied, adding, “Anyhow, finding additional ones this year is hardly probable for me, as I discovered this particular one upon the basement stairs.”
{: #nw-v02-c08-p0058 }

“Robin, what have you done?”
{: #nw-v02-c08-p0059 }

“A toad was placed by me in the bed belonging to Thirza. Should you desire to, you may go and remove it. Yet tell me, Nell, wouldn't leaving it in that spot be entertaining?”
{: #nw-v02-c08-p0060 }

“Robin Farrow!” Nell leaped away from the embrace of Robin and rushed through the hall into the room belonging to Thirza. A bit of disorder showed on the bed. With anxious speed, she pulled away the blankets, and beneath a pillow, blinking its eyes at her, sat the toad beyond all doubt.
{: #nw-v02-c08-p0061 }

“In what way am I able to take that terrible creature outside?” Nell groaned, shuddering. She thought of the fire shovel, so she tiptoed downstairs to retrieve it as Thirza was occupied inside the pantry. Nell encountered her own difficulties transporting the toad down the stairs, because it leaped off the shovel on three occasions, and at one point she believed it was lost inside the hall. Upon lastly leaving it within the cherry orchard, a deep sigh of relief escaped her.
{: #nw-v02-c08-p0062 }

“Should Thirza discover this, she would not feel secure entering her bed for the rest of her days. It brings me great joy that the young wrongdoer showed remorse before it was too late. Isolde is making signs to me over from her window. I am pleased . . . I truly require a bit of distraction, because my nerves have suffered almost everything they can tolerate for a single day between Anthony Tulk being at school and Robin Farrow being at home.”
{: #nw-v02-c08-p0063 }
